files.pskov.md:
# Pskov Checkers

ION implements the standard small board: **37 cells and 13 men per side**. The 61-cell, 24-men arrangement is another documented size, not the board selected here.

## Sources and selected rules

- [Vladimir Makhov, Псковские шашки, 2019 PDF](https://lotos-khv.ru/game/games/pskov.pdf) gives the movement directions, compulsory any-branch capture, Turkish-blocker restriction and an explicit **turn ends at the crown corner** rule.
- [Petkevich’s board/setup and movement diagrams, reproduced and translated by João Neto](https://sagme.blogspot.com/2025/05/hexagonal-checkers.html), document the 37/61-cell sizes, 13/24 starting counts and the single opposite-corner promotion.
- [2013 Tevelev–Sladkov material](https://planet-ka.forum2x2.ru/t535-%D0%9F%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B2%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B8%D0%B5-%D1%88%D0%B0%D1%88%D0%BA%D0%B8) provides the same board sizes and directions but illustrates a Russian-style mid-chain king continuation. That continuation conflicts with Makhov’s explicit stopping rule. ION selects the documented Makhov rule and identifies it in Rules rather than claiming all historical accounts agree.

White starts. Men move one empty edge cell in three forward directions. Capture in all six directions, and complete the selected chain. Any complete chain can be chosen; taking the largest number is not required. Kings fly along all six edge lines and can land on any clear cell beyond the first enemy. Captured pieces block until the full turn ends and cannot be jumped twice.

A man crowns only in the opposite **corner**: d7 for White, d1 for Black on the small board. The crown square ends that turn immediately, even if the new king could capture again. Other far-edge cells do not crown.

The setup is the occupied halfplanes 2r+q≤−2 (White) and 2r+q≥2 (Black), matching the published small diagram with its central empty band. Empty axial positions are preserved; board notation is a–g with d1/d7 at the two tips.

Captured-out or blocked players lose. Agreement and automatic threefold repetition reuse ION’s draw convention. No chess material policy is applied. Automatic repetition is an app adjudication, not a claimed additional Pskov historical rule.

`pskovRules` is an isolated authoritative adapter with create/read/generate/advance/apply/result/view functions. It returns the same complete path/capture/delta contract used by existing CloudBoard selection, persistent game versions, history, sharing and cloud computer dispatch.

# Additional checkers research — 25 October 2026

This records the assigned historical To do entries investigated during ION 0.60. Missing facts are not filled with invented rules, and those To do entries must remain pending.

| Requested entry | Evidence located | Implementation status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pskov Checkers | [Makhov’s illustrated rules PDF](https://lotos-khv.ru/game/games/pskov.pdf), [Petkevich’s small/large diagrams and translation](https://sagme.blogspot.com/2025/05/hexagonal-checkers.html), [Tevelev–Sladkov material](https://planet-ka.forum2x2.ru/t535-%D0%9F%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B2%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B8%D0%B5-%D1%88%D0%B0%D1%88%D0%BA%D0%B8) | Implemented separately in `pskovRules`: 37 cells, 13 men, compulsory any complete capture, flying kings, sole crown corner; the selected published stopping-at-crown rule and conflicting Russian-style continuation account are disclosed in [pskov.md](pskov.md). |
| Warcaby heksagonalne | [BGG’s checkers catalog](https://boardgamegeek.com/wiki/page/Checkers_family) identifies Jacek Sadowski, 1985, 24 men and an n=5 hexagonal grid. | Pending. The linked Polish rules could not be retrieved; exact setup, promotion and capture priorities are unverified. A separate 1973 “Halma i warcaby heksagonalne” product by Gliński is not assumed identical. |
| Les Dames Hexagonales | [Neto’s historical survey](https://sagme.blogspot.com/2025/05/hexagonal-checkers.html) traces it to Boyer/Parton, *Les jeux de dames non orthodoxes et autres jeux à pions* (1956), and discusses the later Damex iteration. | Pending. Original rulebook text and complete arrangement were not available. Damex is not silently substituted for the named older game. |
| Dames hexagonales à trois | [The user’s Escale à Jeux entry](https://escaleajeux.fr/jeu/12jdh) confirms a 91-cell board, three players, 18 men per player and international-draughts principles, tracing the model through *12 Jeux et leur support* to Boyer/Parton (1956). | Pending. The summary does not define exact promotion zones, captures involving two opponents, blocked/eliminated-player handling or the final victory condition. Those multiplayer rules cannot be inferred safely from a two-player draughts engine. |

The research fetched public material only. It did not sign into third-party services, contact publishers, copy their diagrams into ION or publish placeholder games as playable.
